description: Generic software-development rules for front end and back end. Rules without `appliesTo` apply to every ticket; front-end rules apply when the ticket touches a web or mobile surface, back-end rules when it touches api, db, batch or cli. Severity: critical and high are blocking findings, medium and low are actions.

rules.title: Every change traces to the cause or a requirement
rules.check: Each planned change cites the confirmed root cause (bug) or a requirement (feature); nothing unrelated is planned.

rules.title: Fixed values trace to an authoritative source
rules.check: Every fixed value, format, limit and field size the change introduces or relies on traces to a named requirement, spec or existing contract location; anything without an authority is listed as an open question, not guessed.

rules.title: Documented vs actual behaviour is recorded
rules.check: Where the current behaviour differs from the documentation or spec, the plan records the difference and the decision (follow the spec, keep the behaviour, or ask).

rules.title: Related work is checked
rules.check: Open issues, pull requests and recent changes touching the same area are checked for the same defect or overlapping work; the result is reported, also when nothing is found.

rules.title: Every changed condition has a negative case
rules.check: The Condition → negative case table covers every predicate, branch, filter and query condition the plan adds or changes.

rules.title: Side effects and failure behaviour are declared
rules.check: Writes, transactions, locking, migrations, external calls, emitted events and cache invalidations are listed, each with what happens when it fails.

rules.title: Backward compatibility is kept or planned
rules.check: Changed public interfaces (API endpoints, events, data formats, config keys, routes, component props) keep existing consumers working, or the plan names the migration and every consumer to update.

rules.title: Established patterns are reused
rules.check: The plan compares sibling implementations and uses the project's standard mechanism (framework feature, shared module, design-system component); a new mechanism is justified with evidence.

rules.title: Schema changes are reversible and rolled out safely
rules.check: Every schema or data migration has a working rollback (or a stated reason why not), is safe against the data already deployed, and the deploy order with the code is stated.

rules.title: The diff matches the plan
rules.check: Every hunk maps to a plan item; no unplanned behaviour change and no drive-by refactor.

rules.title: Only required schema and data changes ship
rules.check: Every schema, migration or seed change is required by the ticket; changes that were tried and withdrawn are not left in the deliverable.

rules.title: Shared components change only with all consumers checked
rules.check: Shared or base code (libraries, base classes, shared UI components, global styles, common config) is changed only when needed; every consumer is found and verified.

rules.title: Names describe responsibility
rules.check: New and changed names (functions, classes, components, endpoints, files) describe what they do, consistently with their counterparts (interface/implementation, request/response, component/props).

rules.title: Assumptions are enforced where they are relied on
rules.check: Inputs, nullability, ordering, uniqueness and shape that the code relies on are validated at the boundary where they enter (request, form, message, file, props), not assumed.

rules.title: Dependencies are wired the project's way
rules.check: New services, providers, stores or components are registered and injected through the project's standard mechanism, and the wiring is verified by a run or test.

rules.title: Configuration fails closed
rules.check: No environment-specific values are hard-coded; a missing required setting fails clearly instead of falling back to a default that silently selects something else; a renamed key is updated in every consumer.

rules.title: Repository conventions pass
rules.check: The formatter, linter and type checker of the stack pass on the touched files, and new findings are told apart from findings that already existed.

rules.title: Errors are handled, not swallowed
rules.check: New failure paths are handled or propagated with context; no empty catch, no ignored result of a fallible call, no unhandled promise rejection.

rules.title: Ambiguity fails without partial changes
rules.check: When the target of an operation is ambiguous or duplicated, the operation fails before changing anything; duplicates are never collapsed silently.

rules.title: No secrets or personal data in code
rules.check: No keys, tokens, passwords, connection strings or personal data in source, tests, fixtures, client bundles or logs.

rules.title: Data access and commands are injection-safe
rules.check: Queries, shell commands and templates built from input use parameter binding or escaping provided by the stack; no string concatenation with untrusted input.

rules.title: Authorization is enforced on the server
rules.check: New or changed endpoints, jobs and handlers enforce the intended permission checks server-side; tenant and ownership boundaries are checked on every read and write.

rules.title: Untrusted content is rendered safely
rules.check: Untrusted data is rendered through safe bindings (no raw HTML injection without sanitising); client-side checks are treated as UX only; tokens are stored and sent per the project's auth pattern.

rules.title: Multi-step writes are atomic and concurrency-safe
rules.check: Writes that must succeed together run in one transaction; read-then-write sequences on shared data use a lock or a conditional update on the narrowest stable key.

rules.title: Side effects happen after the commit
rules.check: Events, messages, notifications, cache updates and calls to other systems are emitted only after the data they describe is durably committed.

rules.title: Repeated runs are safe
rules.check: Jobs, imports, retries, webhooks and data scripts are idempotent: they use natural keys, handle soft-deleted rows and reject key collisions, so running them twice gives the same result.

rules.title: Audit fields are always populated
rules.check: Created/updated-by and similar audit fields are set explicitly when there is no authenticated user (jobs, scripts, system calls).

rules.title: API contracts stay consistent
rules.check: Request and response shapes, status codes, error format, pagination and naming follow the existing API conventions; the contract (OpenAPI, types, docs) is updated with the change.

rules.title: Every async view handles all states
rules.check: Screens and components that load or submit data handle loading, empty, error and success states, and disable or guard repeated submits.

rules.title: Accessible by keyboard and assistive technology
rules.check: Semantic elements, labels for every input, keyboard operation, visible focus and focus management on dialogs and route changes; images have text alternatives.

rules.title: User-facing text goes through the project's text mechanism
rules.check: Visible strings, dates, numbers and currencies use the project's i18n / formatting mechanism where it exists; no hard-coded copy or locale-specific formats in components.

rules.title: Layout follows the design system and supported sizes
rules.check: Uses the project's design-system components and tokens instead of one-off styles, and works at the supported viewports / devices and orientations.

rules.title: Client state has one source of truth
rules.check: Server data is cached and invalidated through the project's data layer after mutations; no duplicated copies of server state drifting in local component state.

rules.title: No avoidable performance regressions
rules.check: Back end: no N+1 queries, unbounded loops or unpaginated result sets. Front end: no unnecessary re-renders, oversized bundles or blocking work on the main thread. Hot paths are measured when changed.

rules.title: Logs are actionable and safe
rules.check: Logged events are actionable, at the right level, without noise in high-frequency paths, and never contain secrets or personal data; errors carry enough context to diagnose.

rules.title: Comments and docs match the new behaviour
rules.check: Comments, docstrings, READMEs and test descriptions touched by the behaviour change are updated; comment density matches the surrounding code.

rules.title: Logic changes come with automated tests
rules.check: New or changed logic has unit or component tests where the stack has a runner, or the plan says why not; tests fail without the fix.

rules.title: Every plan condition is covered
rules.check: Every Condition → negative case row has at least one positive and one negative test case.

rules.title: Expected results are concrete
rules.check: Each case states a concrete, checkable expected result (value, state, message, screen), never 'works correctly'.

rules.title: Known callers get regression cases
rules.check: Callers and screens named in the impact or investigation have at least one regression case.

rules.title: UI cases cover the supported targets
rules.check: UI cases name the browsers / devices / viewports they run on and include keyboard and error-state paths.

rules.title: Cases were really executed
rules.check: Every case marked OK was executed on its declared surface; the command, trace or recording is attached.

rules.title: Evidence proves the expected state
rules.check: Each OK case has before/after state (data, response, screen) that proves its expected result and is reproducibly tied to the action that produced it; a screenshot alone is not enough.

rules.title: Evidence comes from a controlled environment
rules.check: Cases run in an isolated, known environment; stale workers, caches, queues and locks are cleared before the run.

rules.title: Evidence is regenerated after behaviour changes
rules.check: After any behaviour change, every affected evidence value, capture and expectation is re-derived from a new run.

rules.title: Shared state is restored
rules.check: Every mutation of shared state has a ledger entry and was restored, or the user accepted leaving it.

rules.title: Coverage is reported exactly
rules.check: The run report states measurable coverage (cases planned, run, OK, NG, N/A) and references case ids exactly as in the test cases.

rules.title: Delivery text tells the truth
rules.check: Commit message, PR description and replies state what changed, why and how it was verified, consistent with the final review and evidence; no workflow labels.

rules.title: Only intended paths ship
rules.check: The change set equals the reviewed files; no stray files, logs, local config or generated artefacts.

rules.title: Required formats are kept
rules.check: Deliverables keep their required format (templates, changelog, release notes); fields without a source stay empty rather than invented.

rules.title: Branch is mergeable as reviewed
rules.check: Every dependency of the change exists on the target branch, and concurrent branches touching the same files are checked for conflicts or incompatible changes.

rules.title: Earlier review commitments are honoured
rules.check: Commitments made in earlier review replies on this or related changes are kept, and every claim in the replies is re-verified before delivery.
